title: Provision-to-ready automation: alert inventory + paging policy (DRAFT)
content:
Last updated: 2025-02-27 (draft; thresholds likely to change after we get a clean baseline)

Owner: SRE (Aisha) with Infra Fleet + Control Plane input
Primary audience: SRE oncall, Infra operators running pool bring-ups, Platform/control-plane oncall

---

1) Purpose
We’re adding automation for Dedicated pool bring-up ("provision-to-ready"). This doc proposes:
- The alert inventory (what we alert on, why, how we route)
- Paging policy (what pages vs what creates a ticket)
- Open questions / boundary decisions we need before production rollout

The core goal is to catch “capacity not getting to Ready” and “Ready is unsafe/incorrect” quickly, without paging constantly during normal bring-up churn.

---

2) Definitions / scope
Pipeline states (current working state machine):
Requested → Provisioning → Imaging → Bootstrapping → Validating → Ready
Terminal: Failed (and sometimes Canceled)

Key metrics we assume exist (names are illustrative; see linked Confluence doc for canonical names):
- time_to_ready_seconds{pool_id, region, sku, env} (overall)
- stage_duration_seconds{stage, pool_id, region, sku, env}
- stage_attempts_total{stage, result, reason, env}
- stage_failures_total{stage, reason, env}
- provisioning_runs_total{result, env}
- pools_in_state{state, env} (gauge)

We should be careful with label cardinality:
- pool_id is high-cardinality; OK for logs/events and dashboard drilldown, NOT OK for paging alerts.
- Alerts should aggregate by env/region/stage/reason, and use annotations to link to a dashboard filtered to the specific pool_id/run_id.

Out of scope:
- Serving runtime performance alerts once pool is in routing (handled by existing Dedicated SLO dashboards)

---

3) Alerting principles (draft)
P0 paging alerts MUST mean: “this requires immediate human intervention to prevent or reduce customer impact.”
- For provisioning, customer impact is usually “expansion delayed” rather than “production down,” unless Ready gating is violated (e.g., routing uses a pool not fully validated).

Prefer tickets over pages for:
- Single-run failures that have automatic retries and clear operator UX
- Non-urgent misconfigurations that can wait until business hours
- Known flaky signals we’re still tuning

We need two alert classes:
A) Fleet bring-up health (time-to-ready, stuck stages, failure spikes)
B) Safety/correctness (Ready gating, routing integration, drift detection, perf-canary correctness)

---

4) Proposed paging policy

4.1 Environments
- staging: default is NO paging (ticket only), unless we are actively piloting and explicitly turning on paging for a window.
- prod: paging enabled for safety/correctness and for broad systemic failures.

4.2 Paging vs ticket guidelines
Page (prod):
- “Ready gating is violated” (routing advertising non-Ready capacity)
- “Provisioning system is stuck globally” (multiple pools / multiple regions failing or stuck)
- “Perf-canary/validation is giving false positives/negatives at scale” (risk: routing unsafe pools OR blocking all capacity)
- “Control plane state transitions are broken” (cannot mark Ready/Failed, cannot pause/resume, etc.)

Ticket only (prod):
- Single pool stuck in a stage beyond budget but with clear manual workaround
- Single pool failure with known reason (quota/IAM) and automation already posts actionable status to #eng-infra
- Dashboards missing variables / cosmetic issues

4.3 Proposed routing/ownership
- Fleet provisioning service + IaC orchestration (Terraform apply, imaging): Infra Fleet (Vanessa’s team)
- Control plane state transitions + Ready semantics + routing consumption: Platform Control Plane/Routing (Ethan/Ravi)
- Dashboards/metrics/alert plumbing templates: SRE Observability (Allison/Sergio)

Alert should page the team that can fix it.
If the owning team isn’t on primary oncall, route to SRE primary with explicit escalation instructions (below).

---

5) Alert inventory (draft)

Format:
- Name
- Signal
- Condition (threshold)
- Action (page/ticket)
- Owner (responder)
- Notes / noise risks


A) Safety / correctness (highest priority)

A1. ROUTING_USES_NON_READY_CAPACITY
Signal:
- Metric or event from routing integration: routing_advertised_pools_total{state} or routing_capacity_tokens{pool_state}
Condition:
- Any non-zero advertising/usage where pool_state != "Ready" for > 5 minutes in prod
Action:
- PAGE (prod)
Owner:
- Platform Routing oncall (fallback SRE primary)
Notes:
- This is the "never happen" class. If we see this, we may be actively serving from unvalidated pools.
- Should include annotation linking to Dedicated readiness dashboard filtered to affected pool(s) + run_id.

A2. READY_SET_BEFORE_PERF_CANARY_COMPLETES (regression sentinel)
Signal:
- State transition event ordering checks (control_plane_state_transition_total) + perf_canary_completed_total
Condition:
- count_over_time(ready_transition AND NOT perf_canary_completed)[10m] > 0
Action:
- PAGE (prod)
Owner:
- Control Plane oncall (fallback SRE)
Notes:
- We’ve had a race here during pilot (see PR notes in redwood/pr-48245). Keep this alert during rollout; we can downgrade later.

A3. DRIFT_DETECTED_ON_READY_POOL (high severity if drift affects safety)
Signal:
- drift_detected_total{severity}
Condition:
- severity="critical" AND pool_state="Ready" AND count > 0 for > 10m
Action:
- PAGE (prod) if critical; TICKET if warning
Owner:
- Control Plane / Fleet depending on drift type (see drift reason mapping)
Notes:
- Need a reason → owner mapping. Examples:
  - runtime flags mismatch: Platform
  - helm values mismatch due to bootstrap: Infra Fleet


B) Provisioning pipeline health (systemic)

B1. PROVISIONING_RUN_FAILURE_RATE_SPIKE
Signal:
- provisioning_runs_total{result="failed"} / provisioning_runs_total
Condition:
- failure rate > 25% over 30m AND at least N=4 runs (prod)
Action:
- PAGE (prod)
Owner:
- Infra Fleet oncall (fallback SRE)
Notes:
- Use reason breakdown in annotations (top 3 reasons) to avoid immediate log-diving.
- Ensure “customer-triggered” vs “internal test runs” labeling exists; otherwise we’ll page on chaos testing.

B2. STAGE_STUCK_P95 (global)
Signal:
- stage_duration_seconds{stage} histogram
Condition (prod):
- p95 > stage_budget * 2 over 1h for any stage, and there are >= N pools observed
Action:
- PAGE if stage impacts multiple pools/regions; TICKET if isolated to one region
Owner:
- Depends on stage:
  - Provisioning/Imaging/Bootstrapping: Infra Fleet
  - Validating/perf-canary/control-plane transitions: Platform + SRE
Notes:
- We should avoid alerting on individual pool_id. Alert on aggregate and include a dashboard link listing worst offenders.

B3. POOLS_STUCK_IN_STATE (count-based)
Signal:
- pools_in_state{state}
Condition:
- pools_in_state{state in ["Imaging","Bootstrapping","Validating"]} >= 3 for > 30m (prod)
Action:
- PAGE (prod)
Owner:
- Infra Fleet (Imaging/Bootstrapping), Platform (Validating) — see mapping
Notes:
- This catches “queue backed up” or “state machine stopped advancing.”
- Needs exclusion for planned maintenance windows / paused runs.

B4. TIME_TO_READY_SLO_BURN (provisioning readiness)
Signal:
- time_to_ready_seconds SLI vs SLO target (defined in Dedicated readiness SLO doc)
Condition:
- Fast burn: error budget burn rate > 10x over 1h
- Slow burn: error budget burn rate > 2x over 6h
Action:
- PAGE for fast burn; TICKET for slow burn
Owner:
- SRE primary (triage) + owning team based on top reason
Notes:
- "Error" definition: pool not Ready within target window OR ends Failed.
- Need to agree whether customer-requested expansions only, or include internal pool maintenance.


C) Noise-managed / ticket-only (initially)

C1. SINGLE_POOL_STUCK_STAGE (per-pool)
Signal:
- stage_duration_seconds{pool_id, stage}
Condition:
- Any single pool exceeds budget * 3 for a stage
Action:
- TICKET (prod) + Slack notification to #eng-infra (non-page)
Owner:
- Infra Fleet operator / oncall
Notes:
- We should NOT page on this; we will get paged constantly during early rollout. Slack bot should provide “retry / pause / rerun stage” instructions.

C2. CONFIG_VALIDATION_BREAK_GLASS_USED
Signal:
- config_validation_override_total (break-glass)
Condition:
- any usage in prod
Action:
- TICKET + Security notification (no page)
Owner:
- Infra Fleet (primary) + Security (cc)
Notes:
- This is a “review after” mechanism; pages only if we see repeated usage or correlated incidents.

C3. DASHBOARD_TEMPLATE_VARIABLES_MISSING
Signal:
- dashboard_render_errors_total OR synthetic check
Condition:
- > 0 for 30m
Action:
- TICKET
Owner:
- Observability (Allison/Sergio)
Notes:
- We already had issues with variables not populating for new pool IDs; this shouldn’t wake anyone up.

---

6) Proposed thresholds (placeholders until baseline)
We need to finalize stage budgets from the provision-to-ready overview doc + baseline analysis.
Current placeholder budgets (NOT final):
- Provisioning (IaC): p50 20m / p95 45m
- Imaging: p50 25m / p95 60m (high variance by region/SKU)
- Bootstrapping: p50 15m / p95 30m
- Validating (smoke + perf-canary): p50 10m / p95 20m
- Total time-to-ready target: p95 < 3h (prod) (confirm with Product)

Important: imaging has known regional artifact mirror issues; avoid paging on imaging p95 until we have mirror health signals and/or better retries.

---

7) Routing + notification channels

7.1 Where pages go (draft)
- PagerDuty service: "Dedicated Provisioning" (new)
  - Primary: SRE oncall
  - Secondary/escalation: Infra Fleet oncall, Platform oncall (depending on alert)

7.2 Where tickets go
- Jira internal support (INT) or Linear (TBD); preference is to keep it in the same place we track provisioning work (Linear), but SRE historically uses INT for operational items.
Open question: do we want automatic Linear issues created by alerting? (My vote: yes for ticket-only alerts; easier to tie to ENG project work.)

7.3 Where non-paging notifications go
- Slack: #eng-infra for run status summaries and single-pool problems
- Slack: #eng-sre for alert summary + SLO burn rate (ticket-only)

---

8) Runbook pointers (what every alert should include)
Every alert annotation should include:
- A link to the dedicated readiness dashboard with pre-filled filters: env, region, stage, and a “top impacted pools” table
- A link to the provisioning run detail view (control plane) for affected run_id(s)
- A link to the operator runbook section for the relevant stage
- The correlation ID / run_id, not only pool_id

Canonical runbooks (WIP):
- Dedicated pool provisioning runbook (Infra)
- Control-plane ready state troubleshooting (Platform)

---

9) Open questions (need decisions)

Q1. Who owns stage-level alerts when the symptom is ambiguous?
Example: pools stuck in Validating could be:
- perf-canary harness failure (Perf team / SRE?)
- runtime not bootstrapped correctly (Infra)
- control plane never receiving completion event (Platform)
Proposal:
- Alert routes to SRE primary for first 2 weeks of prod rollout, with explicit playbook to loop in Infra/Platform based on top reason.
- After rollout stabilizes, route directly by stage+reason.

Q2. Should we ever page on a single customer pool being stuck?
- Product/CS may care a lot about one high-visibility customer expansion.
Proposal:
- No automatic paging based on single pool_id.
- Instead, allow an “elevated monitoring” label on a provisioning run (e.g., priority="customer_pilot") that adds Slack notifications + lower thresholds (still ticket-only by default). If we need paging for a specific customer window, do it manually via an oncall note.

Q3. Maintenance windows and intentional pauses
- We are adding pause/resume; paused runs should not count toward "stuck" alerts.
Need:
- pools_in_state should exclude paused, or we add pools_in_state{paused="true/false"}.

Q4. Dealing with retries
- We will have automatic retries/backoff for imaging/bootstrap. Alerts should trigger on "time spent" and "retry count" more than raw failures.
Proposal:
- Add a ticket-only alert: STAGE_RETRY_STORM if retries_total{stage} > X in 30m.

Q5. Noise from region/SKU heterogeneity
- Imaging timeouts on specific SKU/region are known.
Proposal:
- Maintain allowlist of “known slow lanes” (region+sku) with separate thresholds OR a dedicated mirror health check that pages Infra Fleet when mirror is down.

Q6. What is the "definition of Ready" for alerting?
- Do we treat "Validating" as usable by routing? (I believe no; routing must only use Ready.)
This impacts A1 and any “capacity shortfall” alerts.

Q7. Ticket system: INT vs Linear
- SRE likes INT for operational requests; Eng is tracking sprint items in Linear.
Proposal:
- Use Linear for provisioning automation alerts (ticket-only) to keep the feedback loop with ENG-274x work. Use INT only when a ticket needs cross-functional operational handling outside Engineering.

---

10) Next steps
- (Aisha) Align final thresholds with baseline analysis + stage budgets (Week 1 output)
- (Sergio/Allison) Confirm metric names/labels and create alert rules in observability-pack templates
- (Rafael/Vanessa) Confirm ownership routing and PagerDuty escalation targets
- (Ethan/Ravi) Confirm A1/A2 signals exist in routing/control-plane metrics and are low-latency
- Revisit after staging pilot: downgrade/upgrade alerts based on observed noise

Notes to self:
- Once we have a few weeks of data, replace placeholder thresholds with percentile-based alerting + burn-rate.
- Make sure annotations include “what changed recently” links (deploy version / feature flag status), since rollout gating is likely the top root cause early on.
